diagnostic_evidence.quote:
in view of the well-known representation formula of the Smolyak
algorithm (see e.g.,~\cite[Lemma 15.1]{Novak.E_Wozniakowski_book_2})
the total number of point evaluation $N$ can be written explicitly

Let $N$ denote the total number of the function evaluations used
in $S_{\Lambda_{L}}$.

issues.failure_explanation: The claimed equality is false: already for d=1, S_{\Lambda_L}=Q_L^{uni} uses n_L points, not \sum_{\ell\le L} n_\ell. In general the Smolyak combination only involves indices with L-d+1\le|\ell|\le L, and distinct tensor grids built from non-nested Gauss--Hermite nodes may share points (e.g. the origin), so the number of function evaluations is only bounded above by the displayed sum. The two-sided bound (eq:isotropic-N-bound), in particular the lower bound on N needed to pass from n_{L-d+1}^{-\alpha/2} to N^{-\alpha/2}(\ln N)^{\alpha(d-1)/2}, is therefore not justified by the argument given.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the identity by the upper bound N\le\sum_{\ell\in\Lambda_L}\prod n_{\ell_k} and supply a short lower-bound argument for the number of distinct points (e.g. the grids with |\ell|=L each contribute \prod n_{\ell_k}\gtrsim M^{L-d} points with overlaps confined to lower-dimensional coordinate hyperplanes, or count evaluations with multiplicity), giving N\asymp_d M^L L^{d-1}.
issues.overall_effect: The relation N \asymp_d M^L L^{d-1} used in the proof of the isotropic lower bound (and inherited by the isotropic part of Theorem thm:added-1) rests on an incorrect counting identity; the conclusion is still true but unproved as written.
issues.title: Point count N = sum over all of Lambda_L of product of n_ell is not an identity for the Smolyak rule
issues.why_classification: A short, routine counting argument restores the needed asymptotics; the stated rate and all downstream claims survive unchanged.

issues.failure_explanation: For x\ge e^{d-1} the inequality (\ln x)^{d-1}\le x is false in general: with d=4 and x=e^{3}\approx 20.1 one has (\ln x)^{3}=27>x; more generally y^{d-1}\le e^{y} fails at y=d-1 as soon as d-1>e. The stated hypothesis therefore does not yield the asserted intermediate inequality. The needed conclusion \ln N\lesssim_d \ln n_{L-d+1} is nonetheless true (since N\asymp_d n(\ln n)^{d-1} gives \ln N\le \ln C_d+\ln n+(d-1)\ln\ln n), but not by the argument given.

failure_location.quote:
Since $n_{L-d+1}\ge \mathrm{e}^{d-1}$ we have
$(\ln n_{L-d+1})^{d-1}\le n_{L-d+1}$, thus $\ln N\lesssim_{d}2\ln n_{L-d+1}$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the step by the direct estimate \ln N\le \ln C_d+\ln n_{L-d+1}+(d-1)\ln\ln n_{L-d+1}\lesssim_d \ln n_{L-d+1} (valid for n_{L-d+1}\ge 3, say), or strengthen the hypothesis to one that actually implies (\ln n)^{d-1}\le n.
issues.overall_effect: One inference in the proof of the isotropic lower bound (also invoked for the isotropic part of thm:added-1) is invalid; the final estimate is unaffected once the step is replaced.
issues.title: Hypothesis n_{L-d+1} >= e^{d-1} does not imply (ln n)^{d-1} <= n
issues.why_classification: A one-line local correction with d-dependent constants (already allowed by the statement) restores the argument without any loss.

diagnostic_evidence.quote:
where $\mathscr{I}_{\ell}^{\mathrm{uni}}$ is the polynomial interpolation
operator using the zeros of $H_{n_{\ell}+1}$.

Let $n:=n_{\overline{\ell}_{1}}$ denote the number of quadrature
points used in the univariate Gauss--Hermite rule $Q_{\overline{\ell}_{1}}^{\mathrm{uni}}$,
and let $\xi_{1},\dots,\xi_{n}$ be the roots of the univariate Hermite
polynomial $H_{n}$ of degree $n$.

issues.failure_explanation: The identity Q^{uni}_{\bar\ell_1}(p_n)=\int \mathscr{I}^{uni}_{\bar\ell_1}(p_n)\rho requires the interpolation nodes to coincide with the n_{\bar\ell_1} Gauss--Hermite nodes (zeros of H_{n}). As defined, \mathscr{I}^{uni}_{\ell} interpolates at the zeros of H_{n_\ell+1}, so \int\mathscr{I}^{uni}_{\bar\ell_1}(p_n)\rho equals the (n+1)-point Gauss--Hermite rule applied to p_n, which is not Q^{uni}_{\bar\ell_1}(p_n)=0 in general (p_n vanishes at the zeros of H_n, not of H_{n+1}). The displayed equality, and hence the reduction to the integration lower bound, does not hold for the objects as defined.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Either define \mathscr{I}^{uni}_\ell on the zeros of H_{n_\ell} (matching Q^{uni}_\ell), or keep the definition and use the fooling function built from p_{n+1} (zeros of H_{n+1}) together with the (n+1)-point Gauss--Hermite rule; the same lower bound then follows with n+1\le N+1\lesssim N.
issues.overall_effect: The proof of both parts of Theorem thm:added-1 uses an identity that is false under the stated definition of \mathscr{I}^{uni}_\ell; the statement is unproved as written.
issues.title: Interpolation nodes (zeros of H_{n_ell+1}) do not match the quadrature/fooling-function nodes (zeros of H_{n_ell})
issues.why_classification: A local change of the node count (or of the fooling function index) repairs the identity; rates and conclusions are unchanged.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: The value $b$ controls the truncation error, namely the integral of $f\rho$ over $\mathbb{R}^d\setminus [-\boldsymbol{b},\boldsymbol{b}]$, whereas $Q_N$ controls the numerical integration error.

issues.failure_explanation: H^\alpha_\rho contains functions with f\rho decaying only like \rho^{1/2}: e.g. f(x)=e^{x_1^2/4}(1+x_1^2)^{-s} with s>(2\alpha+1)/4 has D^r f\in L^2_\rho for all |r|_\infty\le\alpha, and f\rho\propto e^{-x_1^2/4}(1+x_1^2)^{-s}. Its truncation error \int_{\mathbb{R}^d\setminus[-b,b]^d} f\rho \asymp e^{-b^2/4}b^{-2s-1} equals N^{-\alpha/8}(\ln N)^{-s-1/2} for b^2=(\alpha/2)\ln N, far larger than the claimed N^{-\alpha}(\ln N)^{3\alpha d/2+d/4}. Multiplying f by a smooth cutoff vanishing on [-b,b]^d (bounded H^\alpha_\rho norm, Q_N=0) gives a normalised function whose error is \gtrsim N^{-\alpha/8-o(1)}, so the worst-case bound (eq:aff-lattice-error) is false as stated. Consistently, the decay norm only controls |D^r(f\rho)|\lesssim\rho^{\varepsilon} with \varepsilon<1/2, which forces b^2\ge(2\alpha/\varepsilon)\ln N>4\alpha\ln N; the paper's own Proposition prop:added-2 uses b=2\sqrt{\alpha\ln N}.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Choose b with b^2\ge 4\alpha\ln N (e.g. b=2\sqrt{\alpha\ln N}, or b^2=(2\alpha/\varepsilon)\ln N using the \rho^{\varepsilon} decay bound), redo the truncation estimate explicitly, and recompute the logarithmic exponent from the scaling of the box norm in b; the rate N^{-\alpha} up to a polylogarithmic factor is then recovered.
issues.overall_effect: Proposition prop:lattice-affin is false with the stated truncation parameter; the first row (rank-1 lattice with affine map) of Theorem thm:qmc-summary, which restates it, is unsupported. The other QMC results are unaffected.
issues.title: Truncation box b = sqrt((alpha/2) ln N) is too small: truncation error decays only like N^{-alpha/8}, not N^{-alpha}
issues.why_classification: The statement as written is false and the truncation analysis must be redone with a different parameter and possibly a different logarithmic exponent, but a comparable result (optimal polynomial rate up to logs) is recovered without new architecture.
